title: Environment file: dev, staging, prod
description: One file for each environment, named after it (prod.yaml). Pillars and systems are shared by every environment; this file says what differs.

name.description: Name in the environment picker. Defaults to the file name.

order.description: Where it stands in the picker, lowest first. Ties go by id.

default.description: The environment shown when none is asked for. Without one, the first.

sources.description: Where this environment's numbers come from, by source name. The names metrics and messaging are what the signals use unless a signal says otherwise (see signals); incidents is where open incidents come from. Any other kebab-case name defines a source a signal can be pointed at.

kind.description: The kind of source. Which kinds exist depends on the adapters loaded (the adapters folder beside the program): fake and prometheus are built in, the Azure ones come with the azure adapter. `validate` checks the kind against them. A kind accepted before the adapter that reads it exists shows no data.

connection.description: How to reach it (a workspace, an endpoint). Not used by the fake source.

credential.description: Sources that sign in only: the login to use, by name from credentials. Without it, the one called default, else the kind's usual login (the Azure CLI, az login, for Azure sources).

pollSeconds.description: How often the source is asked. Default 30.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one ask may take before it is given up. Default 10.

credentials.description: How sources sign in, by name. A source without a credential uses the one called default, else its kind's usual login; to change that for all of them, define one called default.

kind.description: The way to sign in; the adapters loaded say which exist. The azure adapter has azure-cli (whoever az login signed in), default (the Azure SDK's usual chain), managed-identity (the identity of the machine it runs on) and service-principal (an app registration).

tenantId.description: The directory to sign in to. Without it, the login's own.

clientId.description: The app registration (service-principal) or user-assigned identity (managed-identity).

clientSecretEnv.description: service-principal only: the name of the environment variable that holds the secret. The secret itself never goes in a registry file.

signals.description: Which source each signal comes from in this environment: a source name from sources, or none. A signal not listed here uses the source called metrics (messaging for backlog and deadLetters). A signal with no source is absent: not shown, not grey.

tenants.description: The tenants of this environment. Each has a database in every system with a tenantPattern.

id.description: Goes into the database name where the tenantPattern has {tenant}.

name.description: What the tenant is called on screen.

kind.description: A test tenant (smoke tests, QA, sandboxes) is drawn paler and striped, can be hidden, and shows amber at worst, never red.

scope.description: How this environment's pillars and systems map onto the cloud: the subscription of each pillar, the workspace, which resources belong to a service and what the telemetry calls each system. Every convention is a rule or a template here; the program assumes none. Templates have {variable} and {variable|filter} holes (filters: nospace, lower, upper); {environment} is this file's id and variables are your own.

inventory.description: The source (from sources) that reads the inventory, a resourcegraph source. Without it, the only one.

workspace.description: The workspace the telemetry is in, a template over {environment} and variables.

variables.description: Your own words for the templates, for example env: prd.

subscription.description: How a pillar finds its subscription: by name or by tag (exactly one). Templates over {pillar} (its scope.code, else its id), {pillarId}, {environment} and variables.

nameLike.description: A wildcard (* and ?) matched, ignoring case, against the subscriptions' names, for example *-{env}-{pillar}.

pillars.description: Pillars named instead of found: pillar id to subscription id.

resources.description: Which resources belong to a service.

name.description: Names the rule in what the inspector shows.

types.description: The resource types it applies to, for example microsoft.web/serverfarms.

pattern.description: A regular expression over the resource's name, ignoring case. Named groups: service (required) is matched with a system's serviceCode; role (api, worker...), pillar, region and tenant are optional.

roles.description: Only systems of these roles. Without it, all.

serviceTag.description: A tag that names the service, for a resource whose name does not match the pattern.

tenantNameTag.description: The tag that holds a tenant's friendly name, on resources whose pattern has a tenant group.

telemetryRole.description: What the telemetry calls a system that has no telemetry.role of its own: a template over {system}, {service}, {name}, {role}, {pillar}, {pillarId}, {environment} and variables.

queries.description: Replaces the inventory source's own queries. {types} in resources stands for the quoted resource types the rules name.

exclude.description: Systems that are not deployed in this environment. They are left out of its town, and an island with no system left is not on the map.

fake.description: Settings for the fake source only.

undeclaredTenants.description: Tenants the fake source finds in the data that the tenants list does not name, so the town can show an unknown tenant.
